# Image v2

<!-- Generated by sdkgen; edit internal/cmd/sdkgen/service_docs.go. -->

Use Gophercloud v2.15.0's image/v2 API through one authenticated service object. Connection manages authentication, region, endpoint interface and TLS.

| Operation | openstacksdk | Go |
|---|---|---|
| Service access | `conn.image` | `conn.ImageV2(ctx)` |
| Optional arguments and defaults | keyword arguments | concrete options and operation-specific `With...Options` |
| Extension inputs | `**attrs`, `**query` | supported `With...Field/Query/Header` options |
| Results | Resource or generator | typed values and errors, or `iter.Seq2` |

Native API coverage and openstacksdk Resource/workflow coverage are tracked separately. Python input aliases are not automatically applied to Go fields. Default responses use Gophercloud models; SDK-owned additions are documented per service. Editing a returned response does not automatically persist it.

Selected stateful resources provide `WaitForState(ctx, ref, target, options...)` and `WaitForDelete(ctx, ref, options...)`. State waits use the service's exact ERROR/error failure defaults and no SDK timeout; deletion observation defaults to 120 seconds, with a 2-second interval. Compute Server `WaitForServer` defaults to ACTIVE and 120 seconds; Cinder Volume/Snapshot `WaitForAvailable` defaults to available. Caller `resource.With...` options apply last. Common `WaitFor/WaitForDeletion` retain their 5-minute default; native `WaitForStatus` has a separate contract. See [wait policies](../../docs/service-waits.md).

`image.Service.UploadImage` uses concrete `ImageUploadOpts` and raw metadata fields for image POST201 followed by binary PUT204. It preserves the creation ImageInfo and both stages' actual bodies, headers and statuses; the caller's borrowed reader is sent once. Creation information survives a later error. See [direct upload](../upload-image.md) for format/private defaults, explicit size, Python automatic size inference, mutable Resource and deprecated upload_image differences.

`image.Service.UpdateImage/SetImageProperties` provides ordered PATCH and add-upsert through concrete `ImagePatch` and property options. The SDK escapes JSON Pointer keys, submits application/openstack-images-v2.1-json-patch once and returns actual200 `ImageInfo`. Empty changes submit [] and observe metadata. See [image updates](../update.md) for field helpers, raw/null/delete values, patch order, property whitespace validation and Python dirty-Resource/coercion/bool-result differences.

`image.Service.GetImage/ListImages/AllImages` uses concrete options and SDK-owned `ImageInfo` for fetch/list. It resolves names or fetches IDs and preserves nullable canonical fields, exact numbers and raw JSON extension properties. Listing validates canonical body next links and retains repeated filters. MaxItems and SinglePage are local consumption policies. See [image reads](../images.md) for omitted/empty/false/zero options, extension filters and response ownership.

`image.Service.ImageTasks/AllImageTasks` requires an image Ref and concrete header/MaxItems options. IDs are used directly and names resolve exactly. One GET returns a finite array of SDK-owned `ImageTaskInfo`, preserving nullable deleted/deleted_at and raw JSON; MaxItems is local consumption. `image.Service.CreateTask/GetTask/Tasks/AllTasks` provides general Task creation, fetch and listing using concrete options and SDK-owned `TaskInfo`. `image.Service.AddImageMember/GetImageMember/UpdateImageMember/RemoveImageMember/FindImageMember/ListImageMembers/AllImageMembers` requires a parent image Ref, literal member ID and concrete header/missing/MaxItems options. Find/Remove default nil IgnoreMissing to true and return nil only after owned GET404/DELETE404 responses are handled successfully. Find fetches an ID directly, without Python's 400/403/list fallback. `image.Service.GetImageCache/QueueImage/CacheDeleteImage/ClearCache/CachedImageNodes/CleanCache/PruneCache` uses fixed cache paths and concrete options. Delete defaults nil IgnoreMissing to true, ignoring only an actual DELETE404 whose body is fully read and closed. Clear's zero target means both cache and queue and omits the header. Clean returns an actual200 opaque response; Prune returns actual200 counts. See [cache](../cache.md) for exact numbers, passive node URLs, target-header ownership, asynchronous server queues and Python version-cap differences. No discovery, active prefetch, automatic fanout or completion inference is added.

`ServiceInfo.ListStores/AllStores(ctx, options...)` lists stores, optionally requesting details with `WithListStoresDetails(true)`. `GetImportInfo(ctx)` reads available import methods and preserves original fields, actual headers and status. `image.Service.DeleteImage(ctx, ref, options...)` deletes an image or the store copy selected by `WithDeleteImageStore`. IDs issue a fixed DELETE directly; names resolve exactly; missing resources are ignored by default. It retains original actual204 response, headers and status without hiding read/close/cancellation errors as absence. See [deletion](../delete.md) for concrete options, store paths, partial results, Python/native success codes and 404 retry differences. Native `Images.Delete` retains its 202/204 contract and resource inventory.

`image.Service.DownloadTo(ctx, ref, writer, options...)` fetches fresh metadata, downloads to the writer in selected store order and checks available checksums. It does not close the caller's writer. It preserves actual metadata/binary responses, bytes written and integrity results. See [downloads](../download.md) for defaults, bounded chunks, checksum priority, partial failures and full200/no-data204 handling. Native `ImageData.Download` retains its stream-result contract.

`image.Service.CreateAndImport` validates concrete metadata/stage/import/wait policy before HTTP, then connects create201, one staging204, fresh fetch200 and import acceptance202. Remote import skips staging; active-state waiting is explicit. See [create/import](../create-import.md) for defaults, option ownership, partial results and Python task/config/cache/cleanup differences. This workflow belongs to the higher-level service from `conn.Image(ctx)` rather than additional versioned native operations.

`ImageData.StageImage(ctx, ref, data, options...)` verifies fresh queued state, sends the caller's Reader once and fetches the image again. `StageKnownImage` uses an existing Image ID/status snapshot to skip the initial GET. Optional Size is an image-size header, not inferred HTTP Content-Length. Actual PUT204 acceptance is separate from the later GET200, and acceptance evidence survives fetch failure. See [staging](imagedata/README.md) for Reader ownership, no replay, partial results and separate import completion. Native Stage/Upload/Download remain available.

`Tasks.WaitForTask(ctx, resource.ID(id), options...)` defaults to success/failure, a 120-second timeout and 2-second interval. It recreates only when a selected failure state and the exact 396 message are observed, using actual fetched type/input; the new ID shares the same context deadline. Native Task Get/Create/List and common waits remain available. See [task waiting/recreation](tasks/README.md) for dedicated options, actual responses, partial results and Python cache differences.

`ImageImport.ImportImage(ctx, ref, options...)` fetches and validates existing image formats before submitting default glance-direct import. `ImportKnownImage` uses an existing native Image ID/format. Concrete options support web/remote imports, root store lists and omitted versus false values, returning the actual 202 response. See [import](imageimport/README.md) for single-store headers, extension fields, partial failure and separate staging/completion waits. Native Create/Get contracts remain available.

`Images.FindIdentity(ctx, identity, options...)` resolves name/ID strings automatically, with list fallback after GET400/403/404, exact ID/name and duplicate checks, and a default missing result of `nil, nil`. Select strict handling with `resource.WithIdentityFindIgnoreMissing(false)`. Caller `WithIdentityFindQuery` filters survive GET and fallback listing; automatic name hints apply only to listing. Concrete options control query/fallback. See [identity finding](../../docs/finding-identities.md) for binding, fixed parents, domain filters and path policy.

[Native task calls](native-tasks.md) describe Glance task create/get/list bodies, omitted queries and next-link rules.

Glance identity finding searches hidden images once after a successful ordinary inventory has no match, applying `os_hidden=true` to the original caller query. The second list gets no automatic name hint or extra GET. Errors, duplicates and cancellation from the first search return immediately; final missing policy applies only after both lists succeed without a match. This maps Python `find_image(name_or_id, ignore_missing=True)`; raw wire queries are a Go extension.

## Go usage

```go
// Inside a function with context.Context ctx and *openstack.Connection conn.
service, err := conn.ImageV2(ctx)
if err != nil { return err }
for value, err := range service.Images.Resources.List(ctx) {
    if err != nil { return err }
    fmt.Println(value)
}
value, err := service.Images.Find(ctx, resource.Name("example"))
if err != nil { return err }
_ = value
```

Examples use standard-library `fmt` and `github.com/JSYoo5B/go-openstacksdk/resource`. Find treats missing resources as errors by default; `resource.WithIgnoreMissing()` returns `nil, nil`. Delete ignores missing resources by default.

Common Collections provide exact name lookup, duplicate-name errors, pagination, context cancellation, and preserved HTTP errors. Wait returns `ErrUnsupported` for resources without status support.

Native-pager `Resources.List/All` and parent-scope `List/All` accept `resource.WithMaxItems(n)` and `resource.WithPaginated(false)` to cap raw rows or consume only the first page. Caps apply before local name/status and Trove user-host filters. Zero is unlimited; negative values fail during lazy iteration before HTTP. Native routes do not send caps as wire limit hints and preserve explicit page sizes, queries, and headers. Full-page extraction may still fail on malformed rows beyond the cap. Existing operation-specific options remain available on native typed List; common consumption options belong to Collections/scopes. See [service list comparisons](../../docs/listing.md) for actual bindings and continuation policies.

## Mutation requests

Pass concrete options to resource Create/Update APIs. Use typed options for standard fields and With...Field for extension fields. Queries and headers use the operation's With... functions. Standard-field/header overrides and unsupported extension mechanisms are rejected before requests. The SDK implements request-builder interfaces.

Operations requiring parents use [scope objects](../../docs/scoped-resources.md), whose Create/Update methods accept the same concrete options. This API reference does not imply support for response tracking or every composite Python cloud operation.

See the [openstacksdk inventory](../../api/openstacksdk/README.md), [complete API reference](../../api/README.md), and [project README](../../README.md) for comparison criteria, Go APIs, and validation.
